title: Identifying the Probability of Root Cause under Partial Precedence Orders
banked_reason: Sound exact cross-order singleton-PRC identification compiler, but D0.5 graded it incremental below the field floor because dense-table complexity does not establish cause-count scalability, evidence remains chiefly a two-cause witness without a substantive application, and adjacent-method priority is unresolved.
gap_reasons: The polynomial bound is measured against the full dense rational table, so it does not establish scalability in the number of causes.
A two-cause witness supports the identification question, but the delivered package lacks a substantive application showing when the certificate changes an analysis in practice.
Its priority relative to adjacent order-sensitive methods remains unresolved.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a sound-and-complete cross-order singleton-PRC invariance certificate over the direct Lu potential-outcome class, with candidate-onward monotonicity, a support-adaptive prefix-state construction, and attainable same-law countermodels when the certificate fails. Mathematical, structural, citation, and maximality reviews passed, but the novelty review graded the package incremental because its polynomial guarantee is relative to a dense exponential input, its main empirical evidence is a two-cause witness, and no substantive application or decisive adjacent-method priority comparison was delivered. A future re-raise should begin from compact-input scalability or sharp order-wide PRC bounds and add a consequential application, rather than re-proving the completed Lu-class lift.
tldr: For a positive rational binary observed law, a precedence poset, and a singleton candidate, the exact compiler decides whether every compatible potential-outcome system satisfying Lu et al. Assumptions 1--3 has the same probability of root cause. It evaluates one root-weighted prefix functional per admissible order, tests local output-annihilator diamonds, returns the common rational value when identified, and decodes two same-law monotone threshold models when it fails. Independent node errors are used for the constructive comparison models, while the identification theorem covers the direct Lu class.
gap: Lu et al. identify PRC after a total causal order is supplied, while partial precedence information may permit several observationally compatible monotone orders. Existing order-bounds, Gaussian CIS, ideal-lattice, and automata results do not directly decide this restricted singleton target.
fill: Establish the prefix causal semantics, binary admissible-order confluence, and an output-sensitive iff certificate with realizable negative witnesses and polynomial bit complexity in the dense input size.
